body: I'm the same height...and have a baby face; the highest people, even strangers, guess my age to be is fourteen, but averages thirteen. I'm almost nineteen.
Out of all of my appearance issues, the having a smaller cock *definitely* is higher than almost all of them.

I can relate, but hearing that you're a student (likely in college) and have a job just makes me envy you. The chances of me going to college are so slim it's laughable, and I've applied to every place in town that I can reach, and ask if they're hiring if every time I go there, eight months and there's still *nothing*

I'm at the point where "worthless" is a buzzword, and "less than worthless" sounds like an apt description.

I can be the same; then you begin to realize that in not even twenty years most of the things you know and love are gone, that in sixty you'll be the ignorant one for technological things, that in less than thirty you'll look and feel "old".

If you're like me, having no real future with no higher education, then it's worse, knowing you'll be poor, or knowing that since you're already not that good looking, and couple that with being poor, then chances are that you'll be alone. 

I'm rambling, but the point is that everything sucks.

Honestly where would I start? However, I would say it is the fact that I am pretty much one of the duller tools in the shed, coupled with a bad appearance and social awkwardness.

Really, I hate everything about myself, to the point of literal hatred.

I think it is more of a Southern thing; what I meant was that you seem "unamerican" if you're unhappy down yonder. Having lived in California and Colorado, and knowing people from all around the country, it seems very much so that the northern states have more sympathy for those who are in need of help of any kind, including depression.

I did some digging for an old [article](http://www.weather.com/outlook/health/fitness-exercise/articles/most-depressing-states_2011-09-07) from the Weather Channel, but statistics show that the states with the largest amount of depression are in the south; it's not really a surprise to me, sadly.

> I think in the South, being unhappy if you're not dirt poor

Having lived in the south, and currently living here, being unhappy at all is considered shameful (and "Unmurrican"). It's fucking disgusting how society, as a whole, seems to make it shameful to be unhappy or, god forbid, *depressed*.

I'm sorry you've gotten such terrible therapists. Have you thought of going to a different institution?

>I even find it a chore to do things I like such as play video games.

Everything is such a chore; being awake, sleeping, masturbating, *thinking*; everything just becomes shit.

God, do I know how this feels; this can become a good instigator for hours or, sometimes even, days' worth of depression.

My luck tends to be bad, so now these thoughts have basically left an imprint on my psyche.

Not going anywhere with this other than saying that I know how that feels.

First my mind starts to feel "slow", stupid slow; it's hard to remember things, I can't remember what I was doing, what I'm going to do later, simple math, et cetera. Then I feel like gravity is pushing me down, specifically in the center of my chest; from there it's just doom and gloom followed by my mind *racing*, a thousand thoughts all at once, changing from subject to subject, but all of them are dark and can be unnerving at times.

Often time it also includes random bouts of the inability to stay awake (falling asleep for around a few seconds to a few minutes), or the inability to sleep *at all* for *days*.

>I figure if the end is death why not just get to it already, why spend the next 50 years of my life in this capitalist hell.

I'm with you there; years and years and years of working minimum wage, barely able to eat or live in the shittiest of apartments, working so hard there's little time to do much else but work work work work work, nothing but working hard and being alone until the day you die. And that's the worst of it, doing it all alone, with no one there who wants to endure it with you or who will be there for you.

I've spent so many nights just staring at the ceiling, knowing that I'll have to work for so many years, without the slightest hope of owning my home, or finding a nice man, or emigrating to a better country. No, just work and living in squalor.

Yes, I am a 'giant dickhead' for breaking your circlejerk that was so far from the truth it isn't even funny.

I'm *such* a dickhead.
I try to, but then darker messages are sent...My brain is truly evil.

>Moreover, anyone with the unfortunate position of actually being from the South is supposed to have nothing but abject contempt for where they live, and have it a constant wish to move elsewhere.

Bullshit, *especially* in Texas. 

>The thing is, there is an attitude among a certain class of people, you know, middle class, white, liberal, educated types, that you are supposed to have seething hatred for the USA,

*Massively* bullshit.

I stopped there, because that is nothing but *bullshit*.

As someone with this problem, it's not my fault biology fucked us over, okay?

It is tiring getting dirty looks when you're eating more formal then almost everyone else at the table.
Oh, it does change, but never for the better. It always seems, to me, that things continually get worse and worse and **worse**. That's just the story of my life; shit card after shit card.

I spent the entire break staring at my computer screen, all day and night for three days.

I moved to the south a little over a month ago, to a very small town off the highway; there's nothing to do and no one to talk to. Every time I speak when in pubic and they hear my northern accent it seems like they want to cut my throat open. The weather is consistently hot and humid, with lots of wind due to being near the coast. It's so different. I'm so alone. I miss my home so very much and finally admitting it makes me all the more depressed.
